items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I didn’t work with Tadd, but I got to know Tadd. ... Tadd came to me after one of the performances and said, “I would like to write something for the band.”

ctx.x: Yeah. It might have come from them. I always loved Tadd’s music. But the guys don’t play Tadd’s music. It’s funny. Good Bait, Our Delight, Ugly Beauty, or something like that. A lot of great compositions. The thing about the jazz musicians, is that they don’t play the jazz musician’s compositions. They play the compositions of the standard composers. But Tadd had a lot of beautiful music that we all should be and should have been playing. He was a very romantic writer. Everything he wrote was
romantic. It’s a kind of an approach to it that would set a mood for some kind of a romantic scene.
